# Message List

## How To Build

A MessageList should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A MessageList should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

The task view of prompt mode: the tasks sent to the harness and their output as the harness works on them.

### Shape

#### Description

Shows tasks and their output, not a conversation. Prompts aren't shown on the right with responses on the left, and tool calls aren't gathered into groups.

#### Sent Prompt

##### Description

A task's header shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled, along with the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Status

##### Description

A task's status is a coloured label that spells it out: "Building" in blue, "Compiling" in cyan, "Running" in yellow, "Done" in green, "Failed" in red, "Cancelled" in orange, and "Not recorded" in grey for a task from the history with no record of its run. The labels are readable in both light and dark mode.

#### Output Table

##### Description

A task's output is a [TaskTableScope](../../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope), whose rows are what the harness did for the task. While the task is under way, its table ends in the waiting row for whatever the harness does next. Tasks never collapse their steps, since their whole chain is of interest.

#### Links

##### Description

Links in the compiled prompt and in reply text are clickable. A link to a file opens it, as the [OpenFileScope](../../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says, and a web link opens in the browser. The file path on a Read, Edit, Write, or MultiEdit row is shown as a link and opens that file the same way.

#### Backgrounds

##### Description

The header for the latest task is coloured like the tab the task was sent from, the colour of its mode, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) body shows for that tab. A task from the history that doesn't say which tab it was sent from keeps the tab bar's colour. The queue along the bottom and the previous tasks row along the top both have the same background colour as the tab bar.
Each task in the previous tasks list hints at the mode it was sent in: its heading's background is a faint tint of that mode's colour, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), red for Code, purple for Chain, blue for Spec, green for Ask, and grey for Freeform, far fainter than the latest task's header, so the list reads as a column of the list's own background with each task only touched by its colour. A task whose mode isn't known, as one from the history that doesn't say, keeps the list's background untinted. Its status label, prompt, checkbox, and buttons stay readab

#### Referenced Spec

##### Description

While a task is running, a [RightSidebarScope](../../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope) slides out from the message list's right edge, listing the spec files the task references, and slides back once the run is over.

#### Scrolling

##### Description

The latest task's table scrolls with its lock to the bottom off to start with, until switched on. Each open project keeps how far its latest task's table was scrolled and whether it was locked, and the rest of its message list as it was left, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says, so switching back to it shows the list just as it was.
However long the list of previous tasks grows, drawing it costs no more than drawing the tasks in view, so scrolling, animations, and new output stay smooth.

##### Scrolling Past

Scrolling carries on past either end of the latest task and the previous tasks, from one to the other, through an elastic stretch at that end. A scroll that reaches an end doesn't stop dead there: the same scroll keeps going, with no pause needed, into the stretch, which resists it, and it crosses over only once it has pushed far enough into the stretch to get past a barrier at its far side. The only scroll that stops at an end is a fling's momentum still running when it gets there, and a scroll that has already crossed over is spent (below).
How the view came to be at its end makes no difference. A scroll begun with the view already resting there, scrolled there some time before, opened there by clicking the previous tasks row, or left there when a slide settled, pulls into the stretch from its very first step, exactly as one that scrolls the view there and carries on; it never has to move the view first, and nothing it does is swallowed by the view before the stretch takes it.
The barrier is a distance to scroll past. The distance a scroll goes past the end builds up, and it crosses over the moment that reaches 768 pixels, about twelve or thirteen notches of a mouse wheel or a firm swipe on a trackpad, however quickly or slowly it gets there, so the end is felt as a real resistance before the view gives way. The scroll that brings the view to its end counts too: whatever of it goes past the end starts the build-up, rather than being lost. Scrolling back the other way takes the build-up down again, and scrolls the view once it is gone.
The build-up never drains while the scroll goes on. A scroll goes on for as long as the wheel or trackpad keeps scrolling, with less than 200 milliseconds between one step and the next, as between the notches of a wheel spun steadily, however slowly; each step adds all of itself to the build-up, so a steady scroll of any speed reaches the barrier and crosses over without being stopped and started again. Only once the scroll has stopped, 200 milliseconds after its last step, does the build-up drain away on its own, back to nothing within half a second of that last step, so a nudge into the stre
The stretch is felt as well as seen. While anything has built up, the view at that end is pulled past its end, following the scroll but by less than it scrolled, and by less the further it is pulled, as a rubber band gives: at the start it moves nearly as far as the scroll, and by the barrier it has been pulled about 64 pixels, never more. Scrolling up at the latest task's top, its header and output move down together, leaving an empty band above them, in the body's colour; scrolling down at the previous tasks' bottom, they move up, leaving the band below them. The previous tasks row and the q
While anything has built up against an end, a glow shows where the crossing will happen: a soft radial glow, centred in the space between the previous tasks row and the queue, fading from its middle to nothing at its edge, in the colour of the mode selected in the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it. It starts small and faint and grows larger and slightly brighter as the build-up nears the barrier, at its largest a little under the height of that space and still only a subtle wash of colour, never
With the latest task's output scrolled to its top, a scroll up past the barrier expands the previous tasks, as clicking their row does, opening scrolled to the bottom, on the tasks sent most recently, as the [HistoryListScope](../../../ui/components/history-list/index.md#history-list-scope) says. Before any task has been sent, or with no previous tasks, scrolling up does nothing more: the view stops at its top without stretching, and no glow shows.
With the previous tasks expanded and scrolled to their bottom, a scroll down past the barrier closes them, as clicking "Back to the latest task" does, bringing back the latest task and its output as they were left.
However the previous tasks are closed, by a scroll or by clicking "Back to the latest task", the latest task's output comes back scrolled just where it was when they were opened, with its lock to the bottom as it was. Locked, it comes back at its bottom and still locked, showing whatever output arrived while the previous tasks were open, and goes on following new output. Unlocked, it comes back at the same place in its output, however much arrived meanwhile; if that place no longer exists, as when the latest task has changed since, it comes back at its top, unlocked.
A fling's momentum still running when an end is reached stops there, never pulling into the stretch or crossing over. Momentum is only what comes after the platform says the fingers have lifted from the trackpad; where it never says, as on Linux, no scroll is taken for momentum, and every one pulls into the stretch. Output or a list too short to scroll is always at both its ends, so any scroll over it that leads somewhere pulls into the stretch. Only the wheel or trackpad crosses over. Scrolling sideways, dragging a scrollbar to an end, and scrolling anything inside that scrolls on its own, su
Crossing over by scrolling is animated, starting from wherever the stretch has pulled the view. Scrolling up, the previous tasks slide down into view from above, already scrolled to their bottom, pushing the latest task's header and output out below them, the two moving together as one column. Scrolling down, the latest task's header and output slide up into view from below, already scrolled where they will settle, pushing the previous tasks out above them. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, as the right sidebar's does. Only the space between the previous tasks row and the queue 
The scroll that crosses over stops at the moment of the switch. The step that takes it past the barrier is used up by the crossing, all of it, however far past the barrier it reached, and none of it scrolls the view beneath. Whatever more of that same scroll follows, as the wheel keeps turning, the fingers keep moving, or a fling's momentum runs on, is swallowed: during the slide and after it has settled, it scrolls neither view, pulls into no stretch, and never crosses back, so the view it switched to is left exactly as it arrived, scrolled where the slide brought it. Only a new scroll moves 

#### Changed Files

##### Description

In a project that is a git repository, every task, the latest and each of the previous tasks, lists the files that changed while it ran, between the two snapshots of the working tree taken as it started and ended, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope)'s task snapshots say. In a project that isn't one, no task shows any of this.

##### List

The files are those `git diff --name-status` gives between the two snapshots, each one added, modified, deleted, or renamed. Each is a row with its path in the project, a small letter for how it changed, A, M, D, or R, in the colour the git panel gives that change, and, for a renamed file, the path it was renamed from, muted, before an arrow. They are listed in path order, below the task's output, beneath the latest task's output table, and beneath an open previous task's table, headed "Files changed" with how many there are. The list is collapsed to its heading to start with, and expands when
While a task is still running, it has only its first snapshot, so it shows no list yet. A task whose run changed nothing reads "No files changed", muted. A task with no snapshots, as one from before they were taken or one whose snapshot couldn't be taken, shows no list.

##### Who Changed

The snapshots catch everything that changed while the task ran, including the user's own edits made meanwhile, as in the side editor. Each file is compared with the files the harness's tool calls reported writing or editing, as the referenced spec works them out, from its file tools and its shell commands, a subagent's included. A file the agent reported is shown as changed by the agent, its row plain; any other is shown as changed during the task, its row muted, with a small clock icon and a tooltip saying it changed while the task ran but not through the agent.

##### Opening

Clicking a file opens its diff between the two snapshots, the file as it was when the task started against the file as it was when it ended, in the [DiffViewScope](../../../ui/components/diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope), as the git panel opens a file's uncommitted changes.

use /lib
from /scope/prompt-mode/ask-conversation import AskConversationScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/modes import PromptModesScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/sending import PromptSendingScope

export shape MessageListFreeformShape:
    description:
        A Freeform task is shown as a regular chat, not as a task: its prompt
        as a message on the right, and the harness's reply as a message on the
        left, read as prose, as the @{AskConversationScope} shows a question
        and its answer.

    conversation:
        While the latest task was sent in Freeform, the space between the
        previous tasks row and the queue shows its conversation as a chat, in
        place of the latest task's header and output table. The chat holds
        the latest task and the Freeform tasks sent straight before it, back
        to the last task of another mode, or to the first that started a new
        conversation, oldest at the top and newest at the bottom. Sending
        another Freeform prompt adds it at the bottom; sending a task in any
        other mode shows that task as ever, and the chat goes with it.

    messages:
        Each prompt is shown as it was typed, in a box on the theme's raised
        surface, faintly tinted Freeform's grey, as the @{PromptModesScope}
        colours it, with corners rounded 6 pixels, set against the chat's
        right edge and at most 80% of its width, with the text and images
        attached to it listed beneath its text. Beneath the box, at its
        right, a small muted line gives the time it was sent and, once its
        task is over, its Resend button, as the @{PromptSendingScope} says;
        while it runs, its Cancel button is there instead. A message sent to
        the task while it ran is a box of its own, laid out the same way,
        placed among the reply where the harness took it in.

        Each reply follows beneath its prompt, against the chat's left edge,
        at the chat's full width, with no box, laid out as the
        @{AskConversationScope}'s answers are: the reply text after the
        harness's last tool call rendered as markdown in the body's text
        colour, everything before it summed up in one small muted line that
        expands into the steps, a status line with a spinner and the latest
        thing the harness did in that line's place while the task runs, and
        the error it failed with, "Cancelled", or "No answer." at its end.
        Beneath the reply, in a git repository, come the files changed while
        it ran, as every task lists them. Prompts are 16 pixels apart, and a
        reply starts 8 pixels beneath its prompt.

        Nothing in the chat is shown as a task: there is no header, no status
        label, no hidden anchor's name, no compiled prompt, and no output
        table.

    scrolling:
        The chat scrolls, opening at its bottom, and stays locked to the
        bottom while it is there, following the reply as it grows; scrolling
        up unlocks it, and scrolling back to the bottom locks it again.
        Sending a prompt scrolls it to the bottom and locks it. It lays out
        only what is in view, however long the conversation. Scrolling past
        its top crosses over into the previous tasks, as scrolling past the
        top of the latest task's output does.

    previousTasks:
        Among the previous tasks, a Freeform task keeps its heading like any
        task's, tinted grey, and opens onto its prompt and its reply laid out
        as they are in the chat, rather than a compiled prompt and a table.

content.text:
The spec now shows Freeform tasks in the message list as a regular chat, laid out like the Ask conversation, instead of a task header and output table. I changed the spec only, not the code; `piton check`, `piton format --check` and `piton build` all pass.

**What changed**

New `spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/Freeform.pi`, `MessageListFreeformShape`, wired into `MessageListShape` as `freeform`:
- **`conversation`:** when the latest task is Freeform, the space between the previous tasks row and the queue shows a chat instead of the header and output table. The chat holds the latest task and the Freeform tasks sent just before it. It goes back to the last task of another mode, or to the first one that started a new conversation, and runs oldest at the top. Sending a task in another mode shows that task in the usual way.
- **`messages`:**
  - Each prompt is a bubble on the right, faintly tinted Freeform's grey, showing it as typed with its attachments.
  - Under the bubble is a muted line with the time, plus Resend once the task is over, or Cancel while it runs.
  - Messages sent to the running task are bubbles of their own, placed where the harness took them in.
  - Each reply is on the left, laid out like Ask answers:
    - prose after the last tool call;
    - one muted line summing up the earlier steps, which expands;
    - a status line with a spinner while it runs;
    - the error, "Cancelled" or "No answer." at the end.
  - Changed files are listed under the reply.
  - Spacing is 16 px between prompts and 8 px from a prompt to its reply.
- **`noTaskTrappings`:** no header, status label, hidden anchor name, compiled prompt or output table.
- **`scrolling`:**
  - The chat opens at the bottom and stays locked there while the reply grows.
  - Scrolling up unlocks it, and sending a prompt locks it again.
  - Only what's in view is laid out.
  - Scrolling past the top still switches to the previous tasks.
- **`previousTasks`:** a Freeform task in the previous tasks list keeps its grey-tinted heading. Opening it shows its prompt and reply in the chat layout.

Other files:
- **`spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.pi`:** the description ("tasks, not a conversation") now names Freeform as the exception.
- **`spec/scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.pi`:** `PromptModesShape.freeform` now says a Freeform task is shown in the message list as a regular chat, where it used to describe its header.

**Choices you may want to change:** "just a regular chat" didn't say which tasks belong in the chat or how replies look. I chose:
- the chat covers the run of consecutive Freeform tasks in the same conversation;
- replies use the Ask pane's style;
- each reply keeps its changed-files list.

**What the code step should follow**
- **`MessageListFreeformShape`** (all properties):
  - In `src/prompt_mode.rs`, when the latest task's mode is `SendMode::Freeform`, render the Freeform chat instead of `render_latest_header` and `render_output`.
  - Reuse the Ask pane's question bubble, answer line, step and answer-piece rendering and `Reply::chat_rows` from `src/prompt_mode/ask_pane.rs`. Its question layout is `question_row`.
  - Tint the bubbles with `mode_color(SendMode::Freeform)`.
  - Keep `scroll_past_ends` working over the chat.
- **`MessageListFreeformShape.previousTasks`:** an open Freeform task in the history list uses the same layout.
- **`MessageListScrollingShape.scrollingPast`:** still applies to the chat's top.

The spec now shows Freeform tasks in the message list as a regular chat, laid out like the Ask conversation, instead of a task header and output table. I changed the spec only, not the code; `piton check`, `piton format --check` and `piton build` all pass.

**What changed**

New `spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/Freeform.pi`, `MessageListFreeformShape`, wired into `MessageListShape` as `freeform`:
- **`conversation`:** when the latest task is Freeform, the space between the previous tasks row and the queue shows a chat instead of the header and output table. The chat holds the latest task and the Freeform tasks sent just before it. It goes back to the last task of another mode, or to the first one that started a new conversation, and runs oldest at the top. Sending a task in another mode shows that task in the usual way.
- **`messages`:**
  - Each prompt is a bubble on the right, faintly tinted Freeform's grey, showing it as typed with its attachments.
  - Under the bubble is a muted line with the time, plus Resend once the task is over, or Cancel while it runs.
  - Messages sent to the running task are bubbles of their own, placed where the harness took them in.
  - Each reply is on the left, laid out like Ask answers:
    - prose after the last tool call;
    - one muted line summing up the earlier steps, which expands;
    - a status line with a spinner while it runs;
    - the error, "Cancelled" or "No answer." at the end.
  - Changed files are listed under the reply.
  - Spacing is 16 px between prompts and 8 px from a prompt to its reply.
- **`noTaskTrappings`:** no header, status label, hidden anchor name, compiled prompt or output table.
- **`scrolling`:**
  - The chat opens at the bottom and stays locked there while the reply grows.
  - Scrolling up unlocks it, and sending a prompt locks it again.
  - Only what's in view is laid out.
  - Scrolling past the top still switches to the previous tasks.
- **`previousTasks`:** a Freeform task in the previous tasks list keeps its grey-tinted heading. Opening it shows its prompt and reply in the chat layout.

Other files:
- **`spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.pi`:** the description ("tasks, not a conversation") now names Freeform as the exception.
- **`spec/scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.pi`:** `PromptModesShape.freeform` now says a Freeform task is shown in the message list as a regular chat, where it used to describe its header.

**Choices you may want to change:** "just a regular chat" didn't say which tasks belong in the chat or how replies look. I chose:
- the chat covers the run of consecutive Freeform tasks in the same conversation;
- replies use the Ask pane's style;
- each reply keeps its changed-files list.

  - Keep `scroll_past_ends` working over the chat.
